claims.text: India and the Visegrad Four (V4) group—comprising Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic—agreed to deepen political, economic, technological, defence, and people-to-people ties.
The Visegrad Four group backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met foreign leaders of the V4 group on the margins of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
India and the V4 nations agreed to establish an Annual Business Forum and hold annual meetings between their foreign ministers.
Slovakia's Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar stated on behalf of the V4 group that India, as an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be a permanent member of the UN Security Council.
The UN Security Council was established in 1945, with China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States holding its five permanent seats.
The Visegrad Group was formed in 1991 in Visegrad, Hungary, following the collapse of the Soviet Union.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar co-chaired the Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace & Prosperity Summit in New York alongside European Council President António Costa.
The Partners for Multilateralism initiative was founded by leaders of the European Union, Brazil, Kenya, and Canada.
A joint editorial by Partners for Multilateralism co-authors noted that 2025 saw state-based armed conflicts across 35 countries and global military spending of nearly $3 trillion.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly General Debate on September 26.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar formally launched India's campaign for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat for the 2028-29 term in July.
Bihar Police filed FIRs against 120 social media account operators for revealing the identity of a minor girl in a viral video.
On September 19, a Class 10 girl and her male friend returning from tuition in Jamui were intercepted, harassed, and sexually assaulted by a group of local youths.
A Special Investigation Team led by female SDPO Deepti Monali was established, leading to the identification of seven suspects and the arrest of three minors.
Jamui SP Bishwajeet Dayal stated police registered an FIR under the POCSO Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita after tracing victims through a vehicle registration number visible in the video.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called the Jamui incident deeply disturbing and demanded that the perpetrators be prosecuted under the POCSO Act.
Bihar Minister Shrawon Kumar drew public criticism for describing the harassment of the minor girl in Jamui as an isolated ('Chhitputh') incident.
JD(U) state president Umesh Kushwaha referred to the Jamui assault as an isolated incident while asserting that law and order was worse prior to 2005.
RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav criticized JD(U) leaders for describing the assault on minors as isolated, calling the incident shameful and a blot on Bihar.
The National Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance of the Jamui incident on September 21, 2026, with Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar directing the Bihar DGP to file an immediate FIR.
Two preterm infants, aged four and five days, died after a fire broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of RIMS hospital in Adilabad, Telangana, around 11:50 p.m. on September 21, 2026.
Adilabad DMHO Dr. Sadhana stated the fire was triggered when an air conditioner in the SNCU reception area caught fire, sending smoke into enclosed glass-windowed wards.
Patient attendants broke glass windows in the unit to clear accumulated smoke and helped evacuate infants.
Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into the fire and instructed officials to strengthen fire safety measures across hospitals statewide.
Adilabad Collector Rajarshi Shah stated 27 newborns were undergoing treatment in the RIMS unit at the time of the fire incident.
Telangana Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha confirmed that the other rescued infants were in stable condition without immediate complications.
IIT Bombay suspended Professor Suryanarayana Doolla from his post as Dean of Administrative Affairs following the suicide of student Sahil Wakode.
Professor Doolla served as an exam invigilator on September 18 when 20-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode was caught using ChatGPT on a mobile phone.
Mumbai Police charged Professor Doolla with abetment to suicide and alleged caste discrimination under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and SC/ST Act.
Faculty bodies from IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, and IIT Madras issued statements supporting Professor Doolla, stating he was following Senate-approved exam rules.
IIT Bombay student representatives issued a statement on September 21 stating their campus protests were aimed at institutional reforms and not at justifying academic misconduct.
IIT Bombay Director Shireesh B. Kedare met with protesting students and signed a document acknowledging a charter of student demands.
Student representatives clarified that asking for Professor Doolla to step down as Dean was a precautionary measure for an independent investigation rather than a presumption of guilt.
IIT Bombay issued an official apology for its initial press statement regarding the circumstances of Sahil Wakode's death, noting it was premature to state details prior to official police findings.
Sahil Wakode's parents alleged that their son was subjected to caste discrimination for three months and threatened with suspension prior to his death.
